               Post-Processing via Dynamic Multi-Expert Fusion

Figure 1. The pipeline of our method. First, the VLM agent analyzes the input image and prompt, selecting expert LoRAs and assigning
weights via an RLHF-tuned adapter. Second, the LoRAs are dynamically merged into the diffusion model by updating only its K and V
matrices. Finally, the adapted model performs the restoration using the image and an enhanced prompt.

paradigms and highlight the superiority of our system.

Figure 3. Qualitative comparison with the SOTA agentic system , illustrating the failures of sequential tool invocation. (a) For an input
with motion blur and JPEG artifacts, the sequential agent aggravates the blocky artifacts. (b) For an input with defocus blur and noise, the
sequential agent catastrophically amplifies the noise . (c) An example of Unrealistic Smoothing. (d) A failure of Content Hallucination,
where the agent generates plausible but non-existent birds. Our system avoids these issues and produces faithful restorations.

                                                                               5. Conclusion
                                                                               In this paper, we proposed a novel VLM-guided one-
                                                                               shot system that redefines the approach to universal
                                                                               photographic post-processing. Our framework, orches-
                                                                               trated by a VLM agent, cooperatively fuses multiple
       LQ              Flux       Flux + Ehanced Prompt   Full Framework       specialized LoRA experts into a diffusion backbone.
                                                                               This single-step, context-aware fusion paradigm directly
Figure 4. Qualitative ablation study on the effectiveness of agent             addresses the core limitations of prior work, namely
components. This figure illustrates the effect of progressively in-            the error accumulation of iterative agents and the poor
tegrating each component on a vertical single-restoration task.                generalization of all-in-one models. Our comprehensive
                                                                               experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance,
                                                                               particularly in challenging zero-shot, real-world scenarios
   We then validate our complete agent-based fusion strat-                     where other methods fail. Future work could explore
egy on the Group 2 dataset, which features coupled degra-                      expanding the library of expert “pens”, investigating the
                                                                               VLM’s role in local, region-based expert fusion, scaling
dations. As shown in Table 5, we conduct a comprehensive
                                                                               the human preference dataset to improve robustness on
ablation to isolate the contributions of our DPO-optimized                     out-of-distribution degradation combinations, and con-
weight allocation and the K-V-only LoRA adaptation strat-                      ducting comprehensive user studies to further validate
egy. We compare four distinct methods: Fixed Weights                           perceptual quality. We believe this agentic, modular,
(K-V only), which merges the LoRAs using fixed, uniform                        and extensible framework represents a significant step
weights as a baseline; Full LoRA (QKV) + DPO, which                            towards truly universal and intelligent image restoration.
